 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. Around the time of the NFL trade deadline, fans are looking for their team to make moves. Depending on the circumstances, they may want their team to go all in for this season, or trade their veteran players for future assets like draft picks.
 What often goes overlooked are the logistics of the trade deadline, notably what happens to a player when they get traded. Is the player whisked off immediately on the next available flight? Is it the responsibility of the former team or the new team to make arrangements?
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement The best source for this information would be someone who has lived it. Former NFL linebacker Kyle Van Noy took to X to explain how it all goes down . In 2016, Van Noy, who was on the Lions at the time, got a call from the general manager informing him that he had been traded. Funnily enough, Van Noy says it wasn't until the end of the conversation that he found out who he had been traded to.
 After the phone call, he explains that the new team wants to get you in as quickly as possible, often on the soonest possible flight. The reason is because the traded player has to take a physical with the new team, and only then can the trade become official.
 Van Noy explains that many of the "real life" hassles that normal people go through when moving are still applicable even for a pro athlete. If you rent an apartment, you still have to pay that month's rent, even though you are no longer living there. If you have a house, you have to contact your realtor to get it on the market. He did say that the former team helped with moving expenses, like shipping his car to the new city. They will also cover the cost of a hotel room until a permanent new place is found.
 Sometimes as fans we forget that professional athletes are human beings just like us. While they have fame and money, they still go through the trials and tribulations that come with a major life change. They change jobs just like we do, and can be blindsided by a change in the same way. Van Noy's insight peels back the curtain and is a reminder that a trade involves far more than a player changing uniforms. The next time your team makes a deadline move, remember that the player being dealt is packing up their life and starting over in a new city, often on a moment's notice.
